segments.note: The emitting-code header example retains the binding instruction, while prefer[2] and avoid[2] retain maintenance on rename and the stale-reference anti-pattern.

activation.note: Read with the given adoption gate, activation covers non-test implementation references and emitting source, including unchanged unresolved headers and plan renames. Either adoption signal suffices; absence of both disables the capability regardless of profiles. String literals, tests, block comments and markup exclusions match the source. Declaration checking is explicitly LLM-judged rather than falsely attributed to the grammar/resolution validator; additional observation needs are disclosed.

audit.summary: All source segments survive at their claimed destinations, with declaration, concrete syntax and resolution expressed as one source-to-plan binding obligation. Exceptions and reasons remain intact; the shared strict-disposition node contains genuinely generic policy, and the application-shaped example is inherited from the source rather than introduced as a scope restriction.

segmentChecks.note: The shared strict-disposition node preserves strictness and accurately states the generic fail-on-every-finding policy, with no advisory mode or ratchet baseline.
The header-above-emitting-code example preserves the binding instruction; prefer[2] and avoid[2] preserve updating bindings after plan renames and avoiding stale URNs.
The non-test scope, exact line-comment URN grammar, optional measure, and binding to the item actually emitted are all retained across then, prefer, avoid, and verifier_detail.
Then and verifier_detail[2] preserve resolution to a JSON registry entry under telemetry/<theme>/<artifact>/ whose id equals the referenced URN.
The declaration obligation remains operative for every emitted item, including the no-header case, and its review-based verification is explicitly identified.
Resolution failure is preserved distinctly: a grammatical URN must match an existing tracking-plan item id, including after renames.
The two-part adoption gate and inert behavior when neither signal exists are preserved, including independence from profiles.
Block comments and markup attributes are expressly excluded from parsing in avoid, activation, and verifier_detail.

risks: The coder-facing text does not define the syntax of an acceptance telemetry declaration, so adoption could be unclear in a repository without a telemetry root.
The labeled URN pattern does not specify token-level character rules; a coder constructing an unusual URN should copy the tracking-plan item id and rely on the validator for edge cases.

unobservable: Whether non-test source emits telemetry and lacks a header naming each emitted item is explicitly LLM-judged rather than mechanically observable.
Acceptance files containing telemetry declarations require a new repository observer.
bun_telemetry_code grammar and resolution findings require a new observer before Datalog can consume them.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the source-to-plan binding obligation, concrete URN grammar, resolution requirement, exclusions, and adoption gate; the compressed fix guidance and shared strict policy are appropriate. Coder-facing guidance is clear, while activation is not fully deterministic because emission review and two observer-dependent facts remain explicitly non-mechanical. I agree with the auditor's PASS verdict.
